posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
I've played three games each in Atlantis and Insula, and not a single hero was incapacitated in any of them.  (Granted, none of those games were against, say, Iron Legacy.)  In my experience, the dinosaurs gnaw on the villain's minions far more often than they threaten the heroes; about the only damage we ever take is from Rivers of Lava.  And Atlantis is dangerous, but also potentially hugely rewarding; Font of Atlantean Power gets 3-5 free hero cards and only one free Villain one, and Pillars of Hercules is practically like giving each hero a second turn in exchange for one Villain card.  Unless I was fighting the Matriarch, I'd virtually always take that trade.  Plus the Krakens, like Velociraptors, are more likely to pick off the villain's mooks, or even finish the Villain himself, than to endanger a hero.

The only Environment I really fear so far is Time Cataclysm, just because of how brain-melting it is.  The others might be dangerous, but usually hurt the villain team at least as much as the heroes.  Plague Rat is actually really interesting for being able to immunize himself from enviro damage.  Should try him in Rook City sometime, see if it can manage to make me sweat.

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Any time the Pillars of Hercules comes out, we try to get rid of it ASAP - having the villain get a free card play at the start of every single turn can be very horrible. Imagine if you were fighting Apostate and at the start of the lart hero's turn he pulled an Apocalypse, and that hero didn't have any Ongoing desctruction? Ouch. Or if Akash'Bhuta played a Primeval Eruption which chained into a whole bunch of other stuff. And if she did that on each of the hero turns...wow, that could get crowded fast. Could be fun, though, in a totally insane kind of way ;). I suppose the Pillars has the potential to be useful against someone like the Chairman, though, if he hasn't flipped yet and it brings out an Underboss which you manage to destroy before his turn comes around. Or Citizen Dawn, if she's flipped and you need enough Citizens to come out so that she'll flip back on her next turn.

The Matriarch, on the other hand...<shudder>. Even worse if the Mystical Defences are out.
